value.rationale: The sharp threshold is the first parameter where a canonical one-dimensional wandering vector for a quadratic finite Blaschke multiplier loses cyclicity. It completely classifies all real weights alpha>-1 and all a in [0,1), includes the nontrivial boundary equality case, and counts every additional interior obstruction. This motivated exact phase diagram bridges the recent Beurling threshold/finite Blaschke problem and reproducing-kernel zero geometry; it is neither a routine monomial case nor a generic rescaling of the global shift theorem.
